definitions.explanation: The largest member of the deer family, living in the northern forests of North America, Europe and Asia; the males have broad, flat antlers. British English calls it an elk, American English a moose.

examples.japanese: ヘラジカ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大|おお}きい→大きい：00335_ookii⟧。
⟦カナダ→カナダ：30077_kanada⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧ヘラジカ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}た→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: I saw a moose in Canada.

examples.japanese: ヘラジカ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧オス⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{手|て}のひら→手のひら：05294_tenohira⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ような⟦{平|ひら}たい→平たい：06671_hiratai⟧⟦{角|つの}→角：02158_tsuno⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}っている→持つ：00478_motsu⟧。
examples.english: Male moose have flat antlers shaped like the palm of a hand.

notes:
Written {箆鹿|へらじか} in kanji: the antlers are shaped like a spatula ({箆|へら}). Also called ムース in books and zoos.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{鹿|しか}→鹿：04347_shika⟧: deer — the general word
- ⟦トナカイ→トナカイ：28135_tonakai⟧: reindeer, caribou — another northern deer, kept in herds
- エルク: in Japanese usually the North American wapiti, not the moose; the English word "elk" is ambiguous
